target_customer: Small and medium businesses in Nigeria and wider Africa, later positioned at structured African businesses with payroll and larger volumes
problem: African SMEs juggle banking, invoicing, payroll and inventory in separate tools. The founder describes the product as 10 percent banking and 90 percent software.
business_model: Fintech and SaaS with business accounts through partner banks, cards, loans and invoice financing
product_category: SME banking and business management software

founders.name: Frederik Obasi
previous_startups: Ran earlier technology and media businesses in Nigeria (names not given in the opened source)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch describes him as a serial entrepreneur who struggled to manage operations and banking at once.

founders.name: Chioma Ugo
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch (2021-09). The YC page lists only Obasi.

founders.name: Rodney Jackson-Cole
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch (2021-09). The YC page lists only Obasi.

competitors.name: Mercury
competitors.what: US startup business banking; TechCrunch notes Prospa is compared with it, a comparison the CEO rejects

competitors.name: Ramp
competitors.what: US corporate card and spend management; named in the same comparison

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating partner bank accounts, invoicing, catalogs and payments is standard fintech engineering, with compliance and bank partnerships the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: Businesses that run invoicing, catalogs and payroll on the platform face switching costs, but banking is delivered through partner banks, so licensing is not owned.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or acquiring Prospa. The company reports still operating business banking with loans and cards in 2025.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reports tens of thousands of businesses on the platform growing 35 percent month on month, over 150,000 product catalogs and 360,000 invoices by September 2021, which shows demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses getprospa.com, a prefixed domain, because prospa.com belongs to an unrelated Australian lender.

identity.logo: not described by an opened source
identity.voice_and_tone: Positions itself as banking for businesses shaping tomorrow (company site).

brand_strength.rationale: Known mainly through funding press. The name is shared with an unrelated Australian lender, which blurs search results. No mascot or community evidence.

outcome_analysis: Prospa raised the largest pre seed in sub Saharan Africa at the time, 3.8M in September 2021, on reported fast growth across SMEs. It is active and the YC page lists about 70 staff. No later priced round was found, so its trajectory after 2021 is unclear; it still operates in 2025 and has moved to target larger structured African businesses.
notes: The pre seed is stated by TechCrunch and listed by Nairametrics, TechCabal and others in search results. YC lists the location as London while most sources say Lagos. CB Insights total of 3.93M is unverified. The Thinkfarm naming and rebrand results are about an unrelated Australian lender called Prospa and are excluded. Mercury and Ramp are comparisons the CEO rejects and the source is dated six months after the batch.
